:::{#thm-inverse-transpose}
#### Inverse of a transpose

If $\matr{A}$ is an invertible $p \times p$ matrix,
then $\tp{\matr{A}}$ is invertible, and

$$\inv{\tp{\matr{A}}} = \tp{\paren{\matr{A}^{-1}}}$$

:::

::: proof

Multiply $\tp{\matr{A}}$ by the candidate inverse on each side:

$$
\ba
\tp{\matr{A}}\,\tp{\paren{\matr{A}^{-1}}}
&= \tp{\paren{\matr{A}^{-1}\matr{A}}}
&& \text{(transpose of a product)}
\\
&= \tp{\matr{I}_p}
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{A}^{-1} \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{I}_p
&& \text{(} \matr{I}_p \text{ is symmetric)}
\ea
$$

$$
\ba
\tp{\paren{\matr{A}^{-1}}}\,\tp{\matr{A}}
&= \tp{\paren{\matr{A}\matr{A}^{-1}}}
&& \text{(transpose of a product)}
\\
&= \tp{\matr{I}_p}
&& \text{(definition of } \matr{A}^{-1} \text{)}
\\
&= \matr{I}_p
&& \text{(} \matr{I}_p \text{ is symmetric)}
\ea
$$

So $\tp{\paren{\matr{A}^{-1}}}$ satisfies @def-matrix-inverse for $\tp{\matr{A}}$.
The first step of each display is @thm-transpose-product.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-inverse-transpose}
#### Inverting a transpose

For
$\matr{A} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
@exm-invertible-matrix gives
$\matr{A}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 0.5 & -0.5 \\ 0 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$,
so @thm-inverse-transpose says

$$
\inv{\tp{\matr{A}}}
= \inv{\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}}
= \tp{\paren{\matr{A}^{-1}}}
= \begin{bmatrix} 0.5 & 0 \\ -0.5 & 1 \end{bmatrix},
$$

and multiplying $\begin{bmatrix} 2 & 0 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix} 0.5 & 0 \\ -0.5 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$
out does give $\matr{I}_2$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#cor-inverse-symmetric}
#### The inverse of a symmetric matrix is symmetric

If $\matr{A}$ is symmetric and invertible, then $\matr{A}^{-1}$ is symmetric.

:::

::: proof

$$
\ba
\tp{\paren{\matr{A}^{-1}}}
&= \inv{\tp{\matr{A}}}
&& \text{(inverse of a transpose)}
\\
&= \matr{A}^{-1}
&& \text{(} \matr{A} \text{ is symmetric)}
\ea
$$

The first step is @thm-inverse-transpose.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-inverse-symmetric}
#### Inverting a symmetric matrix

$\matr{S} = \begin{bmatrix} 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}$ is symmetric,
and $\matr{S}^{-1} = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & -1 \\ -1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$
is symmetric too, as @cor-inverse-symmetric says.

:::
